title: Proof is in the pudding
body:
Simply put, this app has worked for me better than other ideas that i have tried when it comes to habit development. 

I have been developing consistency over time, through the gentle and prompts of this app. The interface and design is pleasing, calming, and delightful. 

This app essentially has taken the research from the literature out there (i do love neuroscience and psychology) and applied it in a gamified system that is practical and useable in my daily life, without the habit formation being too overwhelming or unsustainable.
author: Yen Phang

title: pay before testing app
body: App screenshots look promising, but unlike the fabulous app which use apple’s system, I can’t check out this app for free without keying sensitive credit card payment details. Sad, wanted to check out the guided routine timer tracker that used to be included with the fabulous app for free trial- Fabulous app is supposed to have it under “coaching”-> guided activity sessions, but there’s only “discover”, no guided tracking sessions
author: spinnej

title: Already seeing results
body: I’ve never considered myself as someone with ADHD but I do have trouble on focusing on one work task at a time with much to do and many distractions, and I already use the Fabulous app so thought I’d give this a try. It’s been effective for me this week as I put my 2-3 main tasks in the centred plan for the day and then the deep focus room allows me to stay in the zone with calming white noise and a timer. To support this I’m using tricks recently learned from Fabulous like keeping a distractions and observations note for every session, and putting a special deep work focus type on my phone to turn off notifications. You can’t stop people asking you questions or meetings in the calendar, but I still got a lot more done.
